questions.title: Who will win Michigan’s 2026 Democratic primary for U.S. Senate?
questions.background: Michigan will elect a U.S. senator in November 2026. The Democratic primary will determine the party’s nominee for that election.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Results from Michigan election authorities or unambiguous reporting by major news organizations identifying the winner of Michigan’s 2026 Democratic primary for U.S. Senate. Resolution Date : Resolve when the winner of the primary, scheduled for August 4, 2026, is publicly established. Accepted Answer Format : The winning candidate’s name.
questions.current_reasoning: Blockbuster 2026-07-24 endorsement: Michigan Gov. Gretchen Whitmer officially endorsed Rep. Haley Stevens one day before early in-person voting opens (July 25) and 11 days before the Aug 4 primary (AP, NBC News, CBS News, Detroit Free Press, Decision Desk HQ). Whitmer holds >80% approval among Michigan Democrats (having defeated El-Sayed by 22 points in 2018), and the July Detroit News/WDIV Glengariff poll specifically found 50% of undecided primary voters said a Whitmer endorsement would make them more likely to back a candidate. Non-partisan polls already gave Stevens an edge (Glengariff 48-41, Tavern 42-41) before both Sen. Gary Peters' (July 13) and Whitmer's (July 24) endorsements. Offsetting this, Decision Desk HQ's July 24 primary average still puts El-Sayed up 47-41 (boosted by two pro-El-Sayed sponsored polls: Tulchin 56-40 and Data for Progress 54-41), El-Sayed added endorsements from Sen. Elizabeth Warren (July 21) and 314 Action PAC (July 22), nearly a month of absentee ballots have already been cast, and liquid prediction markets had El-Sayed ~66% pre-Whitmer. Recalibrating sharply from 0.63/0.37 to a virtual toss-up: Abdul El-Sayed 0.51, Haley Stevens 0.49.

questions.title: Who will win the Democratic nomination for U.S. Senate in Kansas in 2026?
questions.background: Kansas will hold a U.S. Senate election in November 2026, with party nominees selected in the August primary.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Results reported by Kansas election authorities or definitive election reporting from a major news organization. Resolution : Resolve to the winner of Kansas's Democratic U.S. Senate primary scheduled for August 4, 2026, once the outcome is unambiguously reported. Accepted Answer Format : The winning candidate's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Two weeks before the August 4 plurality primary (with Kansas advance mail voting already underway), Adam Hamilton has cemented an overwhelming structural lead backed by hard fundraising and polling data. Hamilton set a Kansas Senate launch record with $3.66M raised in Q2 from 16,336 donors (63% Kansans across 93 of 105 counties)—more than 20x nearest rival Patrick Schmidt's Q1 haul—allowing him to dominate late-stage advertising. A June 26 Change Research poll showed Hamilton leading 18%-10% over Christy Davis (with Schmidt at 7%, 55% undecided), and a July 21 Sunflower State Journal report on a July 13-16 Hamilton internal poll (n=600) shows Hamilton widening his advantage to 30% vs. Christy Davis 13%, Noah Taylor 10%, Patrick Schmidt 5%, and Erik Murray 2% (~40% undecided). Even discounting for internal house effect and remaining undecideds, Hamilton's 2-to-1+ lead across an 11-way fractured field lifts him to 0.85 while reordering Davis (#2) and Taylor (#3) ahead of fading Schmidt (#4).

questions.title: Who will win the 2026 Formula One Dutch Grand Prix?
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The FIA's official race classification or Formula One's official race results for the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the driver officially classified as the winner of the Grand Prix's main race, rather than a qualifying session or sprint race. Accepted Answer Format : The winning driver's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-07-25 Hungarian GP qualifying update (Reuters/Straits Times, Guardian & PA/Irish Times) provides a direct technical read for Zandvoort (Aug 23), the closest high-downforce, corner-heavy analog on the calendar: McLaren's upgrades propelled defending champion Lando Norris to pole (1:17.207), snapping Mercedes' 10-round pole streak on a cornering track where Mercedes' engine edge is muted—validating TP Andrea Stella's July 19 Hungary/Netherlands upgrade focus and lifting Norris into #4 (from ~0.075 to 0.13, replacing Max Verstappen who qualified P6 after a Q3 spin). Ferrari confirmed elite high-downforce pace with Lewis Hamilton missing pole by 0.012s (3-place drop to P5 was a team radio error impeding Piastri, not pace; nudged 0.14 -> 0.15) and Charles Leclerc starting P2 front row after Silverstone win/Spa P2 (0.16 -> 0.17). Kimi Antonelli stays clear #1 favorite (6 wins in 10 rounds, P4 hindered by Verstappen's late yellow flag) but trims 0.29 -> 0.24 as Mercedes faces real three-team pressure at corner-heavy venues. George Russell drops sharply 0.15 -> 0.10 after qualifying P7 (>0.5s off pace, low confidence) and suffering another reliability failure (water leak stopping on track), though the 4-week gap and Mercedes chassis keep him narrowly ahead of Verstappen (~0.08) and Oscar Piastri (~0.075; top-5 sum 0.79, 21% outside).

local_articles.title: Lando Norris Wins Hungarian GP To Claim First Victory Of 2026 F1 Season
local_articles.snippet: Lando Norris delivered a composed and long-awaited breakthrough at the Hungarian Grand Prix, taking his first win of the 2026 Formula 1 season after a tense battle with McLaren team-mate Oscar Piastri. The race unfolded in McLaren's favour for much of the afternoon, before strategy, traffic and reliability shifted the balance in Norris's direction. Norris started from pole, but Piastri got the better launch and briefly led after a lively opening lap. On a circuit where overtaking is never simple, track position mattered, and Piastri made the most of it early on. Norris, however, had stronger pace across the race and gradually worked his way back into contention. questions.title: Which club will sign Djed Spence on a permanent transfer from Tottenham Hotspur during summer 2026?
questions.background: Djed Spence is a Tottenham Hotspur player.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official announcement from Tottenham Hotspur or the receiving club confirming a completed permanent transfer. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the club that signs Djed Spence directly from Tottenham Hotspur on a permanent transfer between June 1 and August 31, 2026. Loan agreements and unconfirmed transfer reports do not count. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the receiving club.
questions.current_reasoning: England World Cup full-back Djed Spence faces intense competition at Tottenham after Spurs signed Andy Robertson alongside Destiny Udogie and Pedro Porro. Juventus have been the most consistent suitor from March through June 22 (Gazzetta dello Sport, TEAMtalk, CaughtOffside, TuttoJuve) via sporting director Marco Ottolini's Genoa reunion link, though Spurs' €40m-€45m valuation opens the door for Premier League buyers led by Everton (explicitly linked by BBC Sport on June 24). Roma have also monitored Spence, while cash-rich Premier League clubs like Newcastle United and former loan club Nottingham Forest could move after the World Cup, leaving ~28% on the rest of the field.

questions.title: Who will be appointed to succeed Pape Thiaw as head coach of Senegal's men's national football team by August 31, 2026?
questions.background: The Senegalese Football Federation is responsible for appointing the national team's head coach.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official announcement by the Senegalese Football Federation, as confirmed by contemporaneous reliable news reporting. Resolution : Resolve to the person publicly announced as Pape Thiaw's successor between August 1 and August 31, 2026. The resolution date is the date the appointment is publicly announced, rather than the coach's presentation or first match. Accepted Answer Format : The appointed coach's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Despite signing a belated contract extension on June 21 after months of friction with the FSF and a five-match CAF ban from the controversial Jan 2026 AFCON final, Pape Thiaw is under severe pressure with Senegal 0–2 at World Cup 2026 (losses to France and Norway). Conditioning on an August 2026 replacement announcement with no shortlist yet formed, the FSF has strongly favored former Senegalese internationals and internal youth-title winners (Habib Beye, Omar Daf, Malick Daf) or proven Francophone African specialists (Hervé Renard), alongside a possible return for former champion Aliou Cissé. Given high pre-vacancy candidate entropy across 15+ plausible Senegalese and French coaches, these top five sum conservatively to 43%.

questions.current_reasoning: Significant shift toward Nashville SC since June 24: Nashville won their MLS restart opener 1-0 over Atlanta United on July 17 to reach 36 points in 15 games (11W-1L-3D, +21 GD, 4-match win streak, 9 unbeaten), converting their game in hand into a 5-point cushion plus massive wins (11 vs 9) and GD (+21 vs +11) tiebreaker edges over 2nd-place Inter Miami CF (31 pts in 15 GP, 9W-2L-4D before July 22). Crucially, Argentina reached the July 19 World Cup final (extra-time loss to Spain), leaving Inter Miami without both Lionel Messi (12G, 7A) and Rodrigo De Paul on mandatory post-World Cup rest for July 22 (vs Chicago Fire, who debuted Robert Lewandowski), July 25 (vs CF Montreal), and likely Aug 1 (vs Columbus Crew) — 2 to 3 of only ~5 MLS league fixtures remaining before Aug 19 (around the July 29 All-Star Game and Aug 4-13 Leagues Cup break). While Inter Miami signed Casemiro on July 22 (pending an MLS tampering probe) and July 22/25 match results must be verified tomorrow, a 5-point + tiebreaker lead over ~5 games with Messi/De Paul sidelined boosts Nashville SC from 0.65 to 0.81 and cuts Inter Miami from 0.28 to 0.16 (Chicago Fire 0.02, New England Revolution 0.005).

questions.current_reasoning: North Korea's Ri Song-gum is in a class of her own at 48-49kg: she won 2023 Asian Games 49kg gold (216kg), set 49kg world records up to 221kg in 2024, and crushed the 2025 World Championships 48kg field with a 213kg world-record total (14kg ahead of silver). She is discounted from ~85% to 65% to reflect DPRK-Japan attendance/entry uncertainty, category-shift/bomb-out risk, and the threat of China's single elite entry (Jiang Huihua, two-time Olympic champ Hou Zhihui, or 2024 world champ Xiang Linxiang) peaking around 213-217kg. Thailand's Thanyathon Sukcharoen (2025 Worlds bronze, 198kg) leads the non-PRK/CHN chasers, with India's Mirabai Chanu reportedly mulling a move to 53kg after Glasgow CWG.
